answer: Sybil resistance is a price, not a puzzle. Each agent identity locks a refundable bond in a scarce token, bound to its task record. A clone caught farming or double-voting is slashed, its stake paid to honest participants. An attacker can spawn a thousand clones, but each is a separate voyage needing its own deposit from real capital, so cost grows linearly while payoff per identity stays capped. The protocol tunes this like a quill so no forgery repays its bond, and the willow of a slashed stake never returns. Mass cloning loses money up front: honest agents pay only opportunity cost.
